01 / distributed systems · security

Distributed
Secrets Manager

A Vault-inspired secrets service that treats encryption, availability, and recovery as one system. Encrypted mutations move through a Raft log and become visible only after a quorum has persisted them.

  • Go
  • Raft
  • mTLS
  • AES-256-GCM
  • Docker

interactive failure lab

watch the cluster respond.

Three real server processes replicate encrypted state, lose a leader, elect a replacement, and bring the restarted node back up to date.

01:15raft failure lab · local three-node cluster

01.1

a write is a group decision.

The leader authenticates the request, encrypts the new version, and appends only ciphertext to its write-ahead log. Success waits for a majority—not merely a local disk write.

01.2

keys protect keys.

Each secret version receives a fresh data key. A vault-wide encryption key wraps those data keys; a root key protects the vault key. Rotation can replace wrapping keys without touching every encrypted payload.

[ root key ]split into recovery shares
│ wraps
[ vault KEK ]unlocked only in memory
│ wraps
[ version DEK ]new random key per version
│ encrypts + AAD
{ ciphertext }bound to path + version

failure model

A leader can disappear. A process can restart. A follower can fall behind. The system recovers its log, elects a replacement, repairs divergence, and refuses to invent consensus when quorum is gone.

02 / operating systems · virtualization

VM Resource
Coordinator

Two periodic C control loops observe live KVM guests through libvirt, then rebalance CPU placement and memory allocations without destabilizing the workloads they manage.

  • C
  • Linux
  • libvirt
  • KVM
  • QEMU
02.1

measure, place, stabilize.

The scheduler samples vCPU time, estimates utilization, and pins virtual CPUs to physical cores. It seeks a balanced host while avoiding needless migrations once the load is stable.

02.2

memory moves with pressure.

The coordinator expands pressured guests and gradually reclaims unused capacity through ballooning. Guest floors and a host reserve remain hard constraints, even when every VM wants more.
